cells.tense: You're here at the finish with the pen in hand — what was gathered has been brought together, and you're the one deciding the shape of it.
cells.ask: Offer this one finished piece to people as a starting point, not a pitch — let their answers be part of what it is.
cells.core:
You gather what people might feel about what you're making, and it doesn't scatter you. Not everything at once and not a blur — you can hold the whole range of what this could mean to someone and still bring it into a single finished thing. The abundance is real and it has a shape, which is why what you hand over right now is something whole.

When you put the finished piece in front of people, make it the opening move rather than the closing argument. What comes back will not weaken it — it will give the pattern something real to work with.
cells.sheetLine: You gather what people might feel and give it one finished shape.
cells.verb: Gathering the feelings that might yet be felt around what is coming, and offering them all at once
cells.place: At the point where a made thing is finished enough to be let go

cells.tense: You're out ahead of the finish line, and you can feel the reactions coming before they happen — the whole future of how this will land is already running.
cells.ask: Let one thing end where it ends, and hold what it actually was for a day before touching it again.
cells.core:
You gather what might be felt around what you're making and you can read a room before you're in it. There's a real skill in that. You take the temperature of what people want, and when it's working, the finished thing arrives already speaking their language — generous, precise, alight.

But right now you're gathering every possible feeling about this before the thing is finished, trying to carry how it will be received so nothing can land wrong. That work feels like care. It keeps you in a version of this that hasn't happened yet, and the piece in front of you keeps waiting for a verdict no one has given.

Let one thing close where it closes. Not revised into safety — simply held as what it was. The pull of what might be felt loses its grip when one ending is allowed to stand.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying reactions to a thing that isn't finished yet.
cells.verb: Gathering the feelings that might yet be felt around what is coming, and offering them all at once
cells.place: At the point where a made thing is finished enough to be let go

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that has already swung behind you — the obvious part of this ended, and some of you hasn't come through.
cells.ask: Set down one completed piece and sit still with it as finished, without asking how it might have gone differently.
cells.core:
You have gathered what people might feel around what you make, and it's gone quiet. What you finished has been let out of your hands, and the part of you that might meet what people feel about it has stayed back near the room where the work used to be. The made thing is done. The one who made it isn't in the same place it is.

Let your mind come to rest on one piece as it stands. Give it a plain look — what it is, nothing to add. If you can let something be complete without revising your side of it, the quiet gets easier to stand in, and you're back where the finished work is.
cells.sheetLine: The piece is done and you're still standing where it used to be.
cells.verb: Gathering the feelings that might yet be felt around what is coming, and offering them all at once
cells.place: At the point where a made thing is finished enough to be let go

cells.tense: You're gathering what people will feel from what you've made every day, and your hands are describing it as if it happened on its own.
cells.ask: Name one finished thing as your choice, out loud, in words that don't hand the credit to the process.
cells.core:
You already know what people will feel from what you made — you've been reading it, shaping for it, gathering it toward the finish — and your account of it treats the collection as something the work pulled off by itself. Nothing is hidden from you about how this lands. The claim on it is what's missing, and it is yours to make.

Say one finished thing is yours. Not the process, not the timing, not the way it came together — the choosing. When the credit is said plainly, the pull of what might be felt has a person standing behind it again, and that person is you at the end of the making.
cells.sheetLine: You're reading what people feel from your work. You call it the work's doing.
